relevant_files.role: LanguageInfo struct definition with all handler types
Template for ELEMENT_QUERY and DEFUSE_QUERY constants
Workspace dependency declarations for tree-sitter grammars
Integration test patterns for language support

conventions.commits: Conventional commits with DCO sign-off; signed tags for releases
conventions.testing: Unit tests in language module files; integration tests in crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/; test patterns use tree-sitter Parser and QueryCursor for validation
conventions.linting: cargo clippy with deny-level lints: undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used; cargo fmt --check; cargo deny check advisories licenses
conventions.error_handling: thiserror for error types; Result<T> returns; bounds checks on node.end_byte() <= source.len() before slicing

patterns: Each language module defines ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, and optional REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY as &str constants
Handler functions (extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, etc.) take &Node and &str source, return Option<String> or Vec<String>
Language registration in mod.rs::get_language_info() uses exhaustive match with one LanguageInfo struct per language
Extension mapping in lang.rs::EXTENSION_MAP is a &[(&str, &str)] slice of (extension, language_name) tuples
Inheritance extraction walks parent nodes to find class/interface/enum, then extracts field names from specific child nodes
DEFUSE_QUERY uses tree-sitter capture groups (@write.local, @write.assign, @read.usage) to tag definition and use sites
Tree-sitter queries use field names (e.g., node.child_by_field_name("name")) to access structured fields from grammar

related_issues.title: Add PHP language support via tree-sitter-php
related_issues.relevance: Direct scope of this research; requires implementing PHP language handler following existing patterns

constraints: All languages must register in EXTENSION_MAP (lang.rs) with file extensions
All languages must have a match arm in get_language_info() (mod.rs) returning a LanguageInfo struct
All languages must have a module file in crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/ with pub mod declaration in mod.rs
DEFUSE_QUERY is required for languages with local variables and assignments (Java, Python, Go, Rust, C++, Kotlin all have it)
Handler functions must be Option types; None is acceptable for languages without those features (e.g., CSS has no extract_function_name)
Tree-sitter grammar node types and field names must match the actual grammar; verify against node-types.json or grammar.js
test_coverage: Existing language tests cover: element_query compilation and matching (class/function/interface/enum extraction), inheritance extraction (extends/implements), defuse_query write/read site detection, and acceptance tests for directory/file analysis modes. PHP tests must cover: function_definition and method_declaration extraction, class/interface/trait/enum declaration extraction, base_clause (extends) and class_interface_clause (implements) inheritance, and PHP-specific features like anonymous classes and namespaces if applicable.

library_findings.relevant_api: tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE constant; grammar node types: class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration, method_declaration, function_definition; field names: name, body, attributes; child nodes: base_clause, class_interface_clause
library_findings.notes: PHP grammar uses base_clause (not parent_class field) for extends, class_interface_clause (not interfaces field) for implements; enum_declaration uses enum_declaration_list (not declaration_list) for body; all class/interface/trait/enum have name field and body field

library_findings.relevant_api: Language, Node, Query, QueryCursor; methods: child_by_field_name(), named_child(), parent(), kind(), start_byte(), end_byte()
library_findings.notes: Core tree-sitter API used by all language handlers; field-based access is primary pattern for structured grammar navigation

approaches.name: Full PHP Integration with All Handlers
approaches.description: Create php.rs module with ELEMENT_QUERY covering function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration; implement extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, extract_inheritance handlers; add DEFUSE_QUERY for variable tracking; register in mod.rs and lang.rs with .php extension.
pros: Comprehensive feature parity with Java/Kotlin/Go handlers
Supports method receiver detection and inheritance analysis
Enables def-use analysis for PHP code
Handles all PHP declaration kinds (classes, interfaces, traits, enums)
cons: Requires implementing 4 handler functions with PHP-specific logic
Higher test burden (9+ test cases per handler)
More complex inheritance walk due to base_clause/class_interface_clause structure

approaches.name: Minimal PHP Integration (Query-Only, No Handlers)
approaches.description: Create php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY and CALL_QUERY only; set all handler functions to None; add REFERENCE_QUERY and IMPORT_QUERY for basic analysis; register in mod.rs and lang.rs. Similar to CSS but with more query coverage.
pros: Faster implementation (only queries, no handler logic)
cons: No receiver type detection (methods not linked to classes)

approaches.name: Phased Integration (Queries First, Handlers in Follow-up)
approaches.description: Phase 1: Implement ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY; set handlers to None. Phase 2 (future PR): Add extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, extract_inheritance handlers with full test coverage.
cons: Requires two PRs instead of one

recommendation: Approach 1 (Full PHP Integration with All Handlers). This approach achieves feature parity with existing JVM/Go integrations, enables the full range of semantic analysis (inheritance, receiver detection, def-use tracking), and follows the established pattern in the codebase. The medium complexity is justified by the value delivered. The DEFUSE_QUERY is required because PHP, like Java and Python, has local variables and assignments that must be tracked for semantic analysis; omitting it would leave a gap in the analysis capabilities. Implementation should follow the Java handler as a template, adapting field names to PHP's base_clause and class_interface_clause structure.
language_info_struct_citation:
pub struct LanguageInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub language: Language,
    pub element_query: &'static str,
    pub call_query: &'static str,
    pub reference_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub import_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_trait_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defuse_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub extract_function_name: Option<ExtractFunctionNameHandler>,
    pub find_method_for_receiver: Option<FindMethodForReceiverHandler>,
    pub find_receiver_type: Option<FindReceiverTypeHandler>,
    pub extract_inheritance: Option<ExtractInheritanceHandler>,
}
element_query_draft:
(
function_definition
  name: (name) @func_name) @function
(method_declaration
  name: (name) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration
  name: (name) @interface_name) @class
(trait_declaration
  name: (name) @trait_name) @class
(enum_declaration
  name: (name) @enum_name) @class
defuse_query_draft:
(
assignment_expression left: (variable_name (name) @write.assign))
(assignment_expression left: (name) @write.assign)
(variable_declaration declarator: (variable_declarator name: (name) @write.local))
(foreach_statement value: (variable_name (name) @write.foreach))
(catch_clause parameter: (variable_name (name) @write.catch))
(name) @read.usage
inheritance_walk_citation: From tree-sitter-php grammar (common/define-grammar.js and php/src/node-types.json): class_declaration has field 'name' (type: name node) and children base_clause and class_interface_clause (not fields). To extract inheritance: (1) from class_declaration node, call child_by_field_name("name") to get the class name; (2) iterate children to find base_clause node (keyword 'extends' followed by comma-separated names); (3) iterate children to find class_interface_clause node (keyword 'implements' followed by comma-separated names); (4) for each name child in base_clause, extract text and prepend 'extends '; (5) for each name child in class_interface_clause, extract text and prepend 'implements '. Same pattern applies to interface_declaration, trait_declaration (which may have base_clause for extends), and anonymous_class nodes.
